title: UNIT TWO: PEOPLES AND CULTURES IN ETHIOPIA AND THE HORN
content:
ሰላም የEthioFresh ቤተሰቦች! 👋 እንኳን ወደ PART 2 በደህና መጣችሁ። በዛሬው ክፍላችን የቋንቋ፣ የሰፈራ፣ የኢኮኖሚና የሃይማኖት ታሪካችንን አብረን እናያለን አብራችሁን ሁኑ 👇! 🚀

2.3. Peopling of the Region

2.3.1. Languages and Linguistic Processes
There are approximately 90 languages with 200 dialects in Ethiopia and the Horn. Linguists classify the languages of Ethiopia and the Horn into two major language super families: Afro-Asiatic and Nilo-Saharan.

1. Afro-Asiatic Super Family:
Sub-divided into the following families:
• Cushitic: Divided into four sub-branches:
- Northern: Represented by Beja, spoken in northwestern Eritrea bordering the Sudan.
- Central: Agaw, including Awign, Kunfel, Qimant, Hamtanga, and Bilen.
- Eastern: Afar, Ale, Arbore, Baiso, Burji, Darashe, Dasanech, Gedeo, Hadiya, Halaba, Kambata, Konso, Libido, Mosiye, Oromo, Saho, Sidama, Somali, Tambaro, Tsemai, etc.
- Southern: Represented by Dhalo in Kenya and Nbugua in Tanzania.
• Semitic: Sub-divided into:
- North: Ge'ez, Rashaida (spoken around the Eritrea-Sudanese border), Tigre (spoken in Eritrean lowlands), and Tigrigna (spoken in highland Eritrea and Tigray).
- South Transverse: Amharic, Argobba, Harari, Silte, Wolane, and Zay.
- South Outer: Gafat (extinct) and Gurage.
• Omotic: Spoken by groups including Anfillo, Ari, Bambasi, Banna, Basketo, Bench, Boro-Shinasha, Chara, Dawuro, Dime, Dizi, Dorze, Gamo, Ganza, Gayil, Gofa, Hamer, Hozo, Kachama-Ganjule, Karo, Keficho, Konta, Korete, Male, Melo, Nayi, Oyda, Sezo, Shekkacho, Shekko, Wolayta, Yem, Zayse, etc.

2. Nilo-Saharan Super Family:
Includes Anywa, Berta, Gumuz, Kacipo-Balesi, Komo, Kunama, Kwama, Kwegu, Majang, Mi'en, Murle, Mursi, Nara, Nu’er, Nyangatom, Opo, Shabo, Suri, and Uduk.

Dynamic Nature of Language Classification: Language classification is not static. Factors like population movements, warfare, trade, religious and territorial expansion, and urbanization result in intense linguistic processes. Some languages have died out or come in danger of extinction (e.g., Gafat), while others thrived.

2.3.2. Settlement Patterns
The spatial distribution of people in northeast Africa is the culmination of long historical processes.
• Cushites & Semites: Inhabited the area between the Red Sea (East) and Blue Nile (West) since early times.
- Cushites: Evolved to be the largest linguistic group in the Horn, spreading from Sudan to Tanzania.
- Semites: Second largest population; settled in northern, north-central, northeastern, south-central, and eastern parts of the Horn.
• Omotic Groups: Inhabited southwestern Ethiopia along the Omo River basin. (Exception: Bambasi and Boro live in Benishangul-Gumuz, and Anfillo lives in Wallaga).
• Nilotes: Settled largely along the Ethio-Sudanese border. Some Chari-Nile family members (Karamojo cluster) inhabited as far as Lake Turkana.

2.3.3. Economic Formations
Domestication created two interdependent modes of life: arable (crop production) and pastoral farming.
• Pastoral Economy: Predominantly featured in eastern lowlands (Afar, Saho, Somali, Karayu, Borana Oromo). Afar and Karrayu depend on Awash River; Somali depend on Wabi Shebelle and Genale (Jubba) rivers.
• Mixed Farming: Mainstay of highland populations (Cushites, Semites, Northern Omotic groups) since 10,000 BP.
• Specialized Economy & Crafts: Southern Omotic groups practiced pastoralism, fishing, metallurgy, weaving, and crafts.
• Shifting Cultivation: Practiced by Nilotes along Blue Nile and Baro-Akobo rivers (sorghum as staple, plus millet, cotton). Cattle hold high economic/social value, supplemented by apiculture, fishing, and hunting.

👉
በኢትዮጵያና ቀንዱ አካባቢ ወደ 90 የሚጠጉ ቋንቋዎች እና 200 የቋንቋ ዘዬዎች (dialects) ይገኛሉ። እነዚህም በሁለት ታላላቅ Super Families ይከፈላሉ፦
1. Afro-Asiatic Super Family:
- Cushitic: በቆዳ ስፋትና በሕዝብ ብዛት ትልቁ ሲሆን በ4 ይከፈላል (Northern, Central/Agaw, Eastern, Southern)።
- Semitic: በሁለት ይከፈላል፦ North (ግዕዝ፣ ትግሬ፣ ትግርኛ፣ ረሻይዳ) እና South። South ደግሞ Transverse (አማርኛ፣ አርጎባ፣ ሐረሪ፣ ስልጤ፣ ወላኔ፣ ዛይ) እና Outer (ጋፋት - የጠፋ/extinct፣ ጉራጌ) ተብሎ ይከፈላል።
- Omotic: አብዛኞቹ በደቡብ ምዕራብ ኦሞ ወንዝ ተፋሰስ ይኖራሉ (ከባምባሲ፣ ቦሮ እና አንፊሎ በስተቀር)።
2. Nilo-Saharan Super Family: በኢትዮ-ሱዳን ድንበር አካባቢ የሚኖሩ ሕዝቦች (አኙዋክ፣ በርታ፣ ጉሙዝ፣ ኩናማ፣ ኑኤር፣ ሙርሲ ወዘተ) ቋንቋ ነው።
3. የኢኮኖሚ እንቅስቃሴ: በደጋማው ክፍሎች Mixed Farming (እርሻና እንስሳት ማርባት) ሲዘወተር፣ በቆላማው ምሥራቅ ክፍሎች Pastoralism (ዘላንነት) ይከናወናል። የኒሎቲክ ሕዝቦች ደግሞ Shifting Cultivation (ቦታ እየቀየሩ ማረስ) ይከተላሉ።

💡 Exam Hints:
• Largest Linguistic Group in the Horn: Cushitic.
• Extinct Semitic Language: Gafat.
• Omotic Exception Locations: Bambasi and Boro (Benishangul-Gumuz), Anfillo (Wallaga).
• Staple Food of Nilotes: Sorghum (Shifting Cultivation).

😂 ፏ ፈሽ: የጋፋት ቋንቋ እንደጠፋ ስትሰሙ አትደንግጡ፤ በፈተና ላይ መልሱን ካልፃፋችሁት የእናንተ ግሬድ እንዳይጠፋ ተጠንቀቁ! 😜


2.4. Religion and Religious Processes

2.4.1. Indigenous Religion
Includes beliefs and practices followed since ancient times. Distinctive mark: belief in a Supreme Being with powers attributed to sacred natural phenomena.
• Waaqeffanna (Oromo): Belief in Supreme Being Waaqa. Manifested through Ayyana (spirits) including:
- Abdari (plant fertility spirit), Atete (animal fecundity spirit), Awayi (sanctity), Balas (victory), Chato (beasts' defender), Gijare (parental spirit), Jaricha (peace), Qasa (health deity), Ekera (dead ghost at Hujuba/grave).
- Irrecha: Thanksgiving festival held at riverbanks and mountain tops.
- Qallu (male) / Qallitti (female): Religious leaders connecting Ayyana and believers.
- Abba Muda: Anointment father dwelling at Goro-Fugug.
• Hadiya (Fandana): Supreme Being is Wa'a (creator of world/Qoccancho). Eyes represented by Elincho (sun) and Agana (moon).
• Kambata: Negita/Aricho Magano (Sky God); religious officials called Magnancho.
• Gedeo: Supreme Being is Mageno; thanksgiving rite is Deraro.
• Konso: Worship centered on Waaq (Wakh).
• Gojjam Agaw: Supreme Being called Diban.
• Gurage: Waq/Goita (Supreme Being), Bozha (thunder deity), Damwamwit (health goddess).
• Yem: Worshipped Ha’o (Sky God).
• Wolayta: God is Tosa; spirits include Tawa-Awa/Moytiliya (father's spirit at Dufuwa/grave), Micho (goat spirit), Nago (sheep spirit), Gomashera (war spirit), etc.
• Keficho: Supreme Being is Yero; spirit is Eqo. Harvest sacrifice is Dejo.
• Boro: Supernatural power called Iqa. Rituals include Gure shuka (ecological preservation), Shode de’na (unexpected disease), Marrowa shuka (disease prevention/wealth).
• Nuer: Believe in Kuoth Nhial (God in Heaven) coming through rain, lightning, thunder.
• Syncretism: Intermixing and fusion of indigenous beliefs with Christianity and Islam.

2.4.2. Judaism
Practiced by Bete-Israel (formerly known as "Falasha") in northern/northwestern Ethiopia. Practiced Haymanot (different from Rabbinic Judaism). Accounts trace origins to:
1. Tribe of Dan during Exodus (1400–1200 BC).
2. Arrival with Menilek I (son of King Solomon and Queen Sheba/Azeb).
3. Led by Azonos and Phinhas in 6th century AD.
4. Jewish immigrants intermarrying with Agaw.
5. Scholars (Taddese Tamrat, Kay Shelmay) argue they are remnants of Old Testament followers of EOC and local converts.

2.4.3. Christianity
• Became state religion in 334 AD under King Ezana (r. 320–360 AD), who dropped pre-Christian gods (Ares, Arwe, Bahir, Midir).
• Aedesius and Fremenatos (Fremnatos / Abba Salama / Kasate Birhane): Instrumental in conversion. Fremnatos consecrated as first Bishop by Patriarch Atnatewos of Alexandria. (Coptic Church consecrated bishops until 1959 when Abune Basilios became first Ethiopian Patriarch).
• Nine Saints: Arrived during reign of Ella Amida II (478–486 AD) from Byzantine Empire; expanded Christianity, built churches (Debre Damo), translated Bible to Ge'ez.
• Catholic Expansion: Jesuits attempted conversion in 16th–17th century leading to civil war and expulsion in 1632. 19th-century missionaries: Giuseppe Sapeto, Giustino De Jacobis, Cardinal Massaja.
• Protestantism: Introduced by CMS, CMSL, and Wesleyan Methodist Society (Gobat, Isenberg, Krapf).

2.4.4. Islam
• Prophet Muhammad faced opposition in Makkah (610 AD) and sent followers to Aksum. First group led by Jafar Abu Talib.
• Aksumite king Armah (Ella Seham / Ashama b. Abjar / Ahmed al-Nejash) granted asylum and refused bribes from Quraysh.
• Spread peacefully via trade routes:
- Dahlak Islands Route: Established by early 8th century (Sultanate formed by 10th century).
- Zeila Port Route: Main gateway into interior (8th–9th century).
- Key Islamic Centers: Sheikh Hussein (Bale), Sof Umar Cave, Harar, Benadir Coasts (Mogadishu, Brava, Merca).

👉
1. Indigenous Religions (ሀገር በቀል እምነቶች):
- Waaqeffanna: በዋቃ (Waaqa) ማመን። በቃሉ (Qallu/Qallitti) አማካኝነት ከመንፈስ (Ayyana) ጋር ይገናኛሉ። የምስጋና በዓላቸው Irrecha ይባላል።
- Hadiya: Wa'a (ፈጣሪ)። ፀሐይ (Elincho) እና ጨረቃ (Agana) የፈጣሪ ዓይኖች እንደሆኑ ይታመናል።
- Gedeo: Mageno (ፈጣሪ)፣ የምስጋና በዓል (Deraro)።
- Wolayta: Tosa (ፈጣሪ)።
- Syncretism: የሀገር በቀል እምነቶች ከክርስቲያናዊና እስላማዊ እምነቶች ጋር መደባለቅ/መቀላቀል።
2. Judaism (ይሁዲነት): በቤተ-እስራኤል (Bete-Israel) የሚተገበር ሲሆን ሃይማኖታቸው Haymanot ይባላል።
3. Christianity (ክርስቲያን): በ334 AD በንጉሥ ዔዛና ዘመን የመንግሥት ሃይማኖት ሆነ። አባ ሰላማ (ፍሬምናጦስ) የመጀመሪያው ጳጳስ ሆኑ። ዘጠኙ ቅዱሳን (Nine Saints) ደግሞ መጽሐፍ ቅዱስን ወደ ግዕዝ ተረጎሙ። የመጀመሪያው ኢትዮጵያዊ ፓትሪያርክ አቡነ ባስልዮስ (1959) ናቸው።
4. Islam (እስልምና): የመጀመሪያዎቹ ስደተኞች በጃዕፋር አቡ ጣሊብ እየተመሩ በ615 AD አካባቢ ወደ አክሱም መጡ። ንጉሥ አርማህ (ነጃሺ) ከለላ ሰጣቸው። በዋናነት በንግድና በሰላማዊ መንገድ በዘይላ (Zeila) እና በዳህላክ በኩል ተስፋፋ።

💡 Exam Hints:
• Year Christianity Became State Religion: 334 AD under King Ezana.
• First Ethiopian Patriarch: Abune Basilios in 1959.
• First Group of Muslim Refugees Leader: Jafar Abu Talib.
• Main Gateway for Islam to Interior: Zeila Port.
• Definition of Syncretism: Intermixing of indigenous beliefs with Christianity and Islam.
